children: Hero Motors is set to enter the primary market this week with its Rs 1,000 crore initial public offering (IPO), with the issue currently commanding a grey market premium (GMP) of around 29 per cent ahead of its September 16 opening.

The IPO will remain open until September 18, with the anchor book opening on September 15. The company has fixed a price band of Rs 79-84 per share, implying a valuation of around Rs 3,815 crore at the upper end.

At the reported GMP of Rs 24, the implied grey market price is around Rs 108, indicating a potential listing gain of 28.6 per cent over the upper price band. GMP, being an unofficial market indicator, does not guarantee the actual listing price.

The IPO comprises a Rs 600 crore fresh issue and a Rs 400 crore offer for sale. Hero Motors plans to use Rs 190 crore of the fresh proceeds to repay debt, while another Rs 200 crore is earmarked for equipment purchases and capacity expansion at its Gautam Buddha Nagar facility in Uttar Pradesh.

The company operates as an automotive technology and powertrain solutions provider, supplying engineered systems to global automotive and mobility companies. Its customers include BMW and Ducati. Unlike Hero MotoCorp, Hero Motors operates primarily in the business-to-business automotive components and technology space.
Hero Motors reported a significant improvement in profitability in FY26. Net profit rose 72.9 per cent year-on-year to Rs 43.6 crore, from Rs 25.2 crore in FY25.
Revenue increased 9.1 per cent to Rs 1,188.4 crore, compared with Rs 1,089.6 crore a year earlier. The company is scheduled to list on the NSE and BSE on September 23.
